newsitem.title: CHINA: China power plant calls for generator, boiler bids.
newsitem.headline: China power plant calls for generator, boiler bids.

text.p: A Chinese electricity project on Friday invited bids for the supply of two 900 megawatt or 1,000 megawatt turbine generators and two boilers for a new power plant in Shanghai.

In a bid notice posted in the China Daily newspaper, the Shanghai Municipal Electric Power Co and two import firms said most of the contract value of the equipment would be financed by a World Bank loan, with the balance from co-financing.

The bidding process would be governed by World Bank rules, said the notice by the Shanghai firm and its two partners, the China Electric Power Technology Import and Export Corp and the China National Technical Import and Export Corp.
The equipment was required for Shanghai's Waigaoqiao Thermal Power Project, with the first unit expected to go into operation in 2003 and the second in 2004, the bid notice said.

A proven track record would be required from bidders both for the contract to supply the generators and auxiliaries islands, which would include main transformers, house service transformers and water systems, and for the boilers.
A bid security of $4.0 million would be required and the deadline for bids was October 15, the notice said.
